X.note: Clean 3D water and coast, and the battery line is easy to see. The ships are tiny dark slivers with faint smoke, so there is little sense of scale or drama. The subtitle and source text are small for a phone, the leader line points at one ship with no clear purpose, and the last ship is clipped at the bottom right. Four overlays compete: label, location pin, caption and date.

Y.note: Dense, detailed 3D city that reads as Gibraltar at once from the runway and the rock. The big residents figure and the year are large and legible. The terrain textures are smeared and blurry in places, such as the green patches and the dark hillside, and the data looks low-resolution. The source credit and census subtitle are small, and the attribution bar is wide.

why: Y shows a recognizable, richly detailed place with a big, readable headline number, while X's tiny ships and small text give a weaker reveal.
top_fix_for_weaker: Move the camera much closer and lower to the battery line, and scale up or add detail to the hulls so they read as warships. Cut the on-screen text to one large caption in a bigger font, and drop the leader line and the second caption bar.
